miniProject.title: Consensus log with durable authority and replayable counterexamples
miniProject.brief: Replace `loglab`'s promotion controller with a reduced Raft core in `consensus/`, retaining the existing protocol, storage and history boundaries. Establish timing-free safety before measuring progress on your machine, and keep public lab evidence distinct from actual storage recovery and external-resource fencing.
steps: Build the Raft transition core with an invariant ledger, fault model and acceptance, persistence, commit, apply and reply events. Check elections, freshness, prefix matching, backtracking and current-term commitment against the Raft paper and MIT 6.5840 Lab 3A/3B; retain proofs and adversarial traces.

Connect durable term, vote and log state to `storage/`; recover application, applied boundary and client deduplication together. Add snapshots with index, term and recoverable state; check against single-node replay. Retain publication-crash, partial-snapshot, stale-install and retry regressions separately from MIT Lab 3C/3D results.

Implement quorum-confirmed reads after current-term commitment, with fresh round identity and an application barrier for leader and follower service. Check partitioned old leaders, old-round replies and lagging application with the register oracle; retain histories alongside MIT Lab 4A/4B's logged-read baseline and lease-assumption derivation.

Issue committed lock tokens and atomically persist resource fencing with effects; test stale holders across restart and new-owner activation. Independently enumerate joint quorums and trace a transition crash against the paper's activation rules; retain both counterexamples, keeping full reconfiguration optional and the core fixed-membership.

Extend `net/` with explicit timer, message and durable-write completions. Check vote-before-reply ordering against the persistence contract; retain seeded loss, duplication, reordering, partition and restart campaigns plus seed-independent event replay. Include healing, split-vote, pre-vote and transfer traces checked against the thesis's rules without requiring optional extensions.

Monitor every transition using independent historical election, committed-prefix and application ledgers that survive compaction. Plant a double-vote bug and minimize its safety witness, then minimize a bounded stall preserving its request, reachable majority and healing assumptions; retain replay regressions and classify each predicate separately.

After deterministic gates, run repeated matched baseline, leader-partition, restart/catch-up and snapshot campaigns on your machine. Validate counters against hand-counted traces; retain versions, workloads, durability settings, raw histories, invariant verdicts, election/commit/apply/reply distributions, throughput, message/byte costs, snapshot costs, timeouts and incomplete recoveries, distinguishing logical from measured time.
deliverables: The `consensus/` core, durable adapter, read barriers, fenced-resource fixture and explicit assumption and invariant ledger.
Public lab results plus independent `history/` checks, storage-crash tests, joint-quorum enumeration and minimized schedules in `faults/` and `tests/`.
Raw protocol, storage and snapshot traces with repeated matched measurements and bounded-stall diagnosis in `reports/`.

checks.name: MIT 6.5840 Spring 2026 Lab 3: Raft, Parts A through D
checks.note: Retain election, agreement, simulated persistence and snapshot results; keep course-interface adapters or private Go lab solutions separate from language-independent core evidence.

checks.name: MIT 6.5840 Spring 2026 Lab 4: key/value service, Parts A and B
checks.note: Retain logged-read baseline results; these do not replace your fresh-quorum read-barrier, durable-publication or fencing tests.

rubric.pass: Your independent ledgers validate elections, matching prefixes, preserved commitments and ordered application; replay-oracle tests cover storage publication, snapshots and client deduplication beyond the public lab's simulated persistence.
rubric.strong: The planted bug fails before repair and passes afterward on the same minimized schedule; historical monitors still detect violations hidden by step-down or compaction.

rubric.pass: Your register checker validates read histories despite stale rounds and application lag; resource tests enforce durable fencing after activation. Independent quorum enumeration rejects union-majority shortcuts in the joint-transition trace.
rubric.strong: Leader and follower reads share tested barriers; the defense distinguishes grant from resource activation, states lease assumptions, and preserves configuration state in optional reconfiguration recovery tests.

rubric.pass: Recorded events replay without random selection; reduced safety and bounded-stall predicates remain distinct. Hand-counted counters validate repeated matched measurements with named versions, workload, timeouts, costs and invariant verdicts.
rubric.strong: The stall retains environmental preconditions and an explained missing prerequisite; reports separate simulated time from measured distributions and retain incomplete recovery rather than hiding it.

miniProject.feedsInto: Committed log order, read barriers, snapshot recovery and fenced authority feed shard ownership and stream visibility. Replayable counterexamples, joint-quorum arguments and measured recovery costs become capstone correctness and diagnosis evidence.
